scope: Normal-only paired response identification using the 9 explicitly exposed baseline/A/B cases. The R10/R15 thresholds, case membership, comparator identities and all fresh normal/impact cases are immutable. Neither detector nor clock is modified. This is a training stage, not confirmation.
design: A prepares the state too late when used alone. B advances only the normal approach and reduces detached force but compresses too hard while still attached. Find a single pair of bounded task-space coefficients that respects both maxima and release support simultaneously. Do not interpolate moments of the peak: linearly approximate separately the peak in [3.600,3.900), the peak in [3.900,4.100), the last20ms mean and minimum, using the actual three physically distinct arm runs. Maximise the worst predicted margin on those four criteria subject to unchanged G4 and stricter of both R10/R15 force costs. The optimization variables are continuous, data-derived training settings, not release thresholds.
stage1: Solve bounded max-min LP from the three existing physical traces. Freeze and run those 9 normals for actual matching/cost/G4 validation. If all pass, freeze immediately. If the measured force response is different, a single preregistered trust-region linearization over the same 9 supervised cases is allowed only if no uncontrolled saturation/divergence: probe symmetric b +/- .0625 and feasible a +/- .125 (one-sided at bounds) around the first fit, re-solve once within the sampled bounds, retain safety failures independently. No repeat/threshold relaxation. Never call training or repeated observations holdout.
progression: Only actual complete candidate at 22 exposed conditions may unlock the separate fresh-normal group, only complete fresh may unlock protected positive/negative collision pairs. No forced probes during system identification. If any genuine normal regression remains, no adoption.
